intent: Discover exact native profile IDs and installed POSIX shell launchers per selected local/SSH PC without a manual catalog. Keep native Profile separate from Launcher, reset choices by PC/agent, and revalidate before workspace/tab/worktree creation. Preserve default/resume safety, controlled freshness, shell guards, and creation-only links targeting their linked PC.

evidence: Trigger: set PI_CONFIG_DIR=.custom-omp in the bridge and pane environment, create the native profile ~/.custom-omp/profiles/work/agent, and select its discovered work ID. server/agent-profiles.ts:86 includes this profile, and server/index.ts:302 translates the selection into fixed --profile work arguments for native agent.start.

server/conversation.ts:1215:   const profiles = paths.join(home, ".omp", "profiles"); The reported ~/.custom-omp/profiles/work/agent/sessions/session.jsonl is outside that root, so ompSessionStore returns null.
server/conversation.ts:1231-1233 calls ompHeldTranscript when the reported path is rejected and throws ConversationUnavailable("no_session_path") if the fallback finds nothing.

server/omp.ts:35:   return /^[\w.-]+$/.test(profile) && profile !== "." && profile !== ".." ? join(home, ".omp", "profiles", profile, "agent") : null; This fallback ignores PI_CONFIG_DIR even though it receives the foreground process environment, so it looks under the wrong profile directory as well.
server/agent-profiles.test.ts:12 and :23 already exercise discovery using PI_CONFIG_DIR=.custom-omp; the production conversation readers do not share that root resolution.
findings.suggested_fix: Share the native OMP root calculation with transcript resolution. Make ompSessionStore accept the configured native root while preserving its containment and symlink checks, and make ompAgentDir derive PI_CONFIG_DIR from the pane process environment. Add a fixture where discovery offers a custom-root OMP profile and the reported transcript and process fallback both resolve that profile's actual session.
findings.title: Custom-root OMP profiles launch without readable chat history
findings.why_it_matters: Discovery explicitly supports native OMP profiles under PI_CONFIG_DIR, but the conversation reader still accepts only ~/.omp session paths and its process fallback also searches only ~/.omp. With PI_CONFIG_DIR=.custom-omp and a profile under ~/.custom-omp/profiles/work/agent, the new picker offers work and agent.start launches it successfully, yet chat cannot resolve its transcript even when herdr reports the correct absolute session path. The user gets a running agent with unavailable conversation history. This is an interaction between the newly supported discovery root and existing transcript readers.
findings.validation_reason: With PI_CONFIG_DIR=.custom-omp in the bridge and pane environments and a native work profile, newly added discovery (server/agent-profiles.ts:85-86; fixture coverage in server/agent-profiles.test.ts:12-29) offers it and server/index.ts:302 launches --profile work, but server/conversation.ts:1213-1233 rejects its custom-root session and server/omp.ts:26-35 plus server/gjc-runtime.ts:198-218 confine fallback to ~/.omp, yielding no_session_path when no matching default-root store exists; runtime incidence was not measured.

residual_risks: Discovery searches PATH plus ~/.local/bin, ~/.bun/bin and ~/bin, while native agent.start resolves a command in the pane environment. The native-profile HTTP contract uses an agentStart spy; the completed generic SSH integration does not exercise native profile selection with the canonical executable absent from bridge PATH. Fixture QA should establish that canonical CLI/configuration identity at that boundary; this is an unmeasured integration risk, not a proven launch defect. Later appended caller evidence verified five native fixtures with their canonical bin explicitly on PATH; that does not exercise this omitted-PATH boundary. Full native worktree browser completion remains pending diagnosis.
testing_gaps: Discovery guard regression coverage remains incomplete for binary-helper shadowing (an executable non-shell codex-X earlier in PATH than a same-name shell launcher), canonical-help timeout/output bounds and cached capability reuse/no-probe-when-no-profile behavior. Fixture-only tests can assert no later launcher substitution and bounded discovery with launchers retained. Source guards exist; no current failure was demonstrated.

The changed dialogs cancel discovery and scope selections to machine/agent, but no inspected fixture holds PC A discovery across close/reopen or a switch to PC B with overlapping IDs and then releases A. Add that controlled response-order test to protect the explicit stale-fetch isolation requirement. Inspection found the cancellation and machine guards, so this is a regression coverage gap without an established race defect.
